clue.text: The best bit's a different colour

definitions.meaning: the outstanding moment of a match or show
a streak dyed into hair in a lighter shade than the rest

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the finest part of something stands out in another hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the standout moment of an event, and a lighter-dyed streak in the hair.

clue.text: Wear what one's used to

definitions.meaning: clothing, as a monk's or a rider's distinctive dress
a custom or routine someone follows without thinking

explanation.surface: Advice to dress in whatever you are comfortable with.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a garment such as a nun's robe and an ingrained custom.

clue.text: Splendid network in Spooner's writing for character of 28

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped sounds between words, so the two pieces trade parts

parts.note: splendid means grand
a grid is a network of lines

explanation.surface: A fine web written in a curious way yields a figure from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria's Spoonerism here moves the N rather than the opening sounds: GRAND GRID becomes GRAD GRIND. Thomas Gradgrind is the fact-obsessed schoolmaster of Dickens's Hard Times (28).
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gradgrind is a leading character in Dickens's novel Hard Times, the answer to clue 28.

clue.text: Airline man, awfully loud, at loud scene in the old Rift Valley

definitions.text: scene in the old Rift Valley

parts.note: Sir Freddie Laker founded the cut-price Laker Airways

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of loud are mangled into a new order

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: An aviation boss behaves badly and noisily at a famous East African site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles LOUD into UDOL. Lake Rudolf, in Kenya's stretch of the Great Rift Valley, has since been renamed Lake Turkana, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Rudolf was the colonial name of the lake lying in the Rift Valley, now called Lake Turkana.

clue.text: Venus loses by following speaker to call in receivers

indicators.note: following says the trimmed painting comes after the mouth

parts.note: gob is slang for mouth, the organ one speaks with

indicators.note: loses tells us the word by is taken out of the painting's name

parts.note: the Rokeby Venus is Velazquez's famous painting in the National Gallery

explanation.surface: The goddess, or a tennis star, is beaten after following someone's call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venus' is the Rokeby Venus; 'loses' strips BY from ROKEBY to leave ROKE. 'Speaker' sounds like a homophone signal but is just the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To go bankrupt is to be forced to call in the receivers, who wind up an insolvent firm.

clue.text: Theology's restricted subject to Jupiter's work

parts.note: theology cut down to its usual abbreviation is Th, as in a Doctor of Theology's ThD
subject to means under, as in under orders

explanation.surface: Religious study is confined to the work of a Roman god.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter was the Roman sky god who hurled thunderbolts, so the rumbling sky is his handiwork.

clue.text: Give best of iron to Paris

definitions.meaning: to concede or yield to someone's superior judgement
the French words ... mean of iron, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: An iron gift, perhaps the Eiffel Tower, handed to the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To give best is to yield, the same as giving way to someone; the French phrase supplies the same letters.

clue.text: The dead must repeat the same stuff

indicators.note: must repeat says the piece is written twice in a row

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same again

explanation.surface: The departed are doomed to say the same things over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct flightless bird is proverbially dead, as in the idiom about being dead as one.

clue.text: Give up supporting Japanese game

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
go is the ancient board game played with black and white stones, popular in Japan

explanation.surface: A fan of a Japanese pastime decides to abandon it.
explanation.definitionFit: To do without something is to relinquish or give it up.

clue.text: Boy scares holders of polo sticks?

parts.note: Roy is a boy's name
scares means alarms, as a noun or verb

explanation.surface: A lad frightens the players gripping their mallets on the polo field.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on polo as a royal sport: the arms of royals who play it hold the sticks, while the phrase also means a royal coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun: royal arms are a coat of arms, but royals' literal arms grip polo sticks.

clue.text: Illuminated character of 28

definitions.meaning: the Lancashire resort is famed for its autumn Illuminations of coloured lights
Stephen ... is the honest mill-hand in Hard Times

explanation.surface: A lit-up figure from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackpool is a seaside town in north-west England whose Illuminations draw crowds each autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is synonymous with its light displays, and Stephen of that surname is a Dickens weaver.

clue.text: Jump race telescoped by character of 28

indicators.note: telescoped means the two words are pushed together so a shared letter overlaps

parts.note: to jump is to bound
the Derby is the famous flat horse race at Epsom

explanation.surface: A leap and a horse race are squeezed together to form a fictional figure.
explanation.walkthrough: BOUND and DERBY share a D at the join; 'telescoped' slides them together so it appears once.
explanation.definitionFit: Josiah Bounderby is the boastful mill-owner and banker in Dickens's Hard Times.

clue.text: Man, of course, dies to grow afresh

indicators.note: afresh asks for the letters to be made anew in another order

explanation.surface: A plant that withers must regrow from scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afresh' reorders DIESTOGROW. 'of course' is the twist: a man found on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The golfer is the most famous man on a golf course, hence a man of the course.

clue.text: See 9
Potential rebel with 10 in whisky

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the drink

parts.note: malt is short for malt whisky
con is the Italian and Spanish word for with, as in chilli con carne
the numeral 10 is written as the word ten

explanation.surface: A possible insurgent with a tenner in the whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 10 is just the number, not a reference to the clue 10-across.
explanation.definitionFit: A discontented person is someone liable to rebel, a potential rebel.

clue.text: Southerly breeze the French do?

parts.note: S is short for south or southerly
a breeze is a light wind
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Asks whether a warm wind blowing up from the south is a Gallic party.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for cheating them, the same as a swindle.

clue.text: Forbidden to practise breaking stuff with rock

indicators.note: breaking suggests the letters of the two words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A rule bans smashing material with a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' reorders STUFF and ROCK together; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional struck off the register, such as a doctor, is banned from practising.

clue.text: Cock getting one for nothing, one for the oven

indicators.note: one is A and nothing is O, so an A takes the place of an O

parts.note: a cock is a rooster, the male chicken

explanation.surface: A cockerel, swapped for something free, ends up roasted.
explanation.definitionFit: A roaster is a chicken bred or chosen for roasting, a bird destined for the oven.

clue.text: Thence comes the card giver's memory

parts.note: a ref, the referee, shows players yellow and red cards
ROM is read-only memory in computing

explanation.surface: From there arrives a dealer's recollection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card giver' suggests a dealer but is a football referee.
explanation.definitionFit: Thence and the answer both mean from that place or source.

clue.text: Dangerous flower goes to Tannenbaum

definitions.meaning: a flag is an iris, and a red signal flag warns of danger
the socialist anthem is sung to the tune of the German carol O Tannenbaum

explanation.surface: A risky bloom is sent to a German fir tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Flag is the British Labour Party's anthem, sung to the tune of O Tannenbaum.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning signal of danger, and the song set to a Christmas carol melody.

clue.text: Parsley is showy, without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the showy word goes round the point

parts.note: showy means garish, gaudy
N is the north point of the compass

explanation.surface: The herb is flashy but has no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a deletion but means outside here: GARISH wraps N.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsley is the classic example of a garnish, a herb sprinkled to decorate food.

clue.text: Substitute for devil responsible for 28

definitions.meaning: a mild exclamation used in place of devil

explanation.surface: A stand-in for Satan wrote a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the Victorian novelist doubles as a polite euphemism for the devil.

clue.text: Pan (according to "The Wind in the Willows") turns up in canis major

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up reads the phrase from bottom to top

parts.words: Pan (according to "The Wind in the Willows")
parts.note: in Kenneth Grahame's book, Pan appears to Ratty and Mole as the Rat's god, the Piper at the Gates of Dawn

explanation.surface: The god Pan, as a children's classic depicts him, appears among the constellations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses RAT'S GOD. Sirius, the brightest star in the sky, lies in the constellation Canis Major, the Great Dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius is the chief star of the constellation Canis Major, so it is found within it.

clue.text: Business knowledge about tug, scene of 28

parts.note: Co is short for company

indicators.note: about places the tugging word inside the knowledge word

parts.note: ken is knowledge, as in beyond one's ken
to tow is to tug

explanation.surface: A firm knows about a tugboat at the place where a novel is set.
explanation.definitionFit: Coketown is the grim fictional mill town where Dickens's Hard Times takes place.

clue.text: Mound where Charles met Cromwell?

parts.note: K stands for king, as Charles I was
Old Noll was the nickname of Oliver Cromwell

explanation.surface: Asks where the king and Cromwell came face to face.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles I and Oliver Cromwell were enemies in the English Civil War; 'met' just places one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A hillock or small rounded hill is a mound.

clue.text: What keeps leader back is a plant

definitions.meaning: a drag on the head, something slowing whoever is in front
a garden herb or flower of the mint family

explanation.surface: Whatever holds up the boss is a mole planted in the organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as DRAG ON HEAD: a hindrance to the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Dragonhead is a genus of aromatic plants, also called dragon's head.

clue.text: Fiddle turns up on board

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin

explanation.surface: A violin appears on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The game is played by throwing at a dartboard, so it happens on a board.

clue.text: See 20
I wish I could record one way I deal with listeners

parts.note: O to is a poetic way of wishing, as in O to be in England
to log is to record
I is the Roman numeral one
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone wishes they could track one route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O to' is the wish, as in Browning's 'Oh, to be in England'. 'Listeners' are ears.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear specialist treats ears, the organs one listens with.

clue.text: Slip top off — panic

indicators.note: top off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: terror is extreme fear, panic

explanation.surface: An instruction to whip off a top in alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake.

clue.text: Offender reportedly encountered …

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that is said rather than written

parts.note: fell on means came upon or encountered

explanation.surface: A criminal is said to have been met.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has committed a serious crime is a felon.

clue.text: … runs round government department with many a book

indicators.note: round says the running word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: hares means runs fast
the DTI was Britain's Department of Trade and Industry
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many

explanation.surface: Continuing from the last clue, the offender races around a ministry with lots of reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the clue to 27 only in the surface. DTI was a UK government department.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard Times is Dickens's 1854 novel, the theme of this puzzle.
